title: (No AI) The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/gettyimages-2285784039.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world's most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. He also wears a cool leather jacket.

Which makes Huang's [admission that he had an affair](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1029990/jensen-huang-the-spy-who-loved-me) with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy - reportedly _while_ her spying was known to US intelligence and even President Donald Trump - all the more shocking. The fallout goes well beyond his marriage, his reputation, or Nvidia itself. Experts tell _The Verge_ the incident threate …

title: (No AI) ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
author: Jay Peters
content:
![A screen of ChatGPT showcasing the Business Agent feature. ](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Business-Agent-Customer-Conversation.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

ChatGPT is going to let you chat with verified "Business Agents" that represent a brand to help you with things like comparison shopping. The feature, available first to "eligible" e-commerce and online service businesses in the US, is launching as part of a suite of business-focused features in ChatGPT being [announced today in beta](https://openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/).

You can start talking with a Business Agent if a business that has created one appears in a response from ChatGPT. While chatting with a custom agent, you can ask about a business's offerings and ask follow-up questions, like asking about differences between two different products.
